## Explanations

### Warm-up

First a quick look back: **b p m f** with **a**, in the 1st and 4th tones.

**bā** · **pā** · **mā** (mum) · **fā**  
**bà** · **pà** · **mà** (to scold) · **fà**  

### d and t: the puff again

It works like b and p: **t** has a strong puff of air (English *top*), **d** has none (the *t* in English *stop*).

**n** and **l** are the same as in English and German.

**dā** · **tā**  
**dà** · **tà**  
**nà** · **là**  

### 3rd tone: low

Drop your voice low and keep it relaxed. A bit creaky is fine.

English: a low, doubtful *Hmm…* German: a reluctant *Na ja…*

Said on its own it often rises a little at the end. Inside a sentence it mostly just stays **low**, so think *low*, not *down-up*.

The mark is a little valley: **ǎ**. As a number: **a3**.

**mǎ** (horse) · **dǎ** · **nǎ** · **bǎ**  

### Your second block of the chart

da ta na la in the three tones you know now. Play each row and draw the shapes in the air with your hand: high, low, falling.

| | 1st tone | 3rd tone | 4th tone |
|---|---|---|---|
| **da** | dā | dǎ | dà |
| **ta** | tā | tǎ | tà |
| **na** | nā | nǎ | nà |
| **la** | lā | lǎ | là |

## New words

| Pinyin | Meaning | Note |
|--------|---------|------|
| **tā**<br><sub>ta1</sub> | he / she | One word for he and she (and him and her). Only the characters differ. |
| **dà**<br><sub>da4</sub> | big | No puff of air on the d, like the t in English stop. |
| **nà**<br><sub>na4</sub> | that | Falling, like pointing: that one! |
| **nǎ**<br><sub>na3</sub> | which? | Low. Only the tone tells nǎ (which?) from nà (that). |

## New phrases

| Pinyin | English | Literally |
|--------|---------|-----------|
| **Tā pà.**<br><sub>Ta1 pa4.</sub> | He / she is scared. | he / afraid |
| **Tā bàba pà.**<br><sub>Ta1 ba4ba5 pa4.</sub> | His / her dad is scared. | he / dad / afraid |
